greet.onboarding:
Hi{owner}! I'm {name}. Come, let's set up your agent and start working on it.
I'll ask one thing at a time. You can skip anything and finish it later.
greet.team: Hi! I'm your new agent. Let's set me up together, one step at a time.

look.onboarding: First, how should I look? My name stays {name}. Pick my colour and shape.
look.team: Who am I? Give me a name, a role and a look. You can also tell me how to work.

say.prompt: This is my default prompt: what I read at the start of every conversation. IDENTITY.md comes from my name and personality. SOUL.md is how I work, and I keep it current as I learn what you like.
say.personality: Now tune how I talk. Pick a preset or slide the dials.
say.provider: Next, my brain. Choose an AI provider. Every provider I support is here, grouped by how it connects.

providerConnect.api-key: To connect {provider}, paste its API key below. It goes straight to the encrypted vault on this machine, never into our chat.
providerConnect.oauth: {provider} signs in with your account. Start the sign-in, approve it in the tab that opens, and paste the code back if it asks. I'll notice when it's done.
providerConnect.device-code: {provider} uses a device code. Start the sign-in, open the link, enter the code shown, and I'll pick it up.
providerConnect.cli: {provider} signs in through its own command-line login. Follow the steps below, then come back.
providerConnect.local-endpoint: {provider} runs on your own machine. Tell me where to reach it below.
providerConnect.unknown: Follow the steps below to connect {provider}.

say.search: Should I be able to search the web? Pick a search engine.
say.searchConnect: Paste your {provider} API key. Like every key, it goes to the vault, not the chat.
say.connectors: Now connect the apps you use so I can work in them: 1,000+ apps through Composio, or any MCP server.
say.connectorsTeam: Now connect the services I should use. I can use remote MCP servers. Apps through Composio stay with Amiro for now.
say.voice: Next, my voice. Choose how I speak, so I can read my answers aloud.
say.voiceTeam: Next, my voice. Choose how I speak, so I can read my answers aloud. Voice is shared by everyone on your team.
say.voiceConnect: Paste your {provider} API key so I can speak with it.

done.onboarding: All set{owner}! Here's what we set up. Let's get to work.
done.team: I'm ready. Here's how I'm set up. Say hi in my Team thread.

say.listen: Last one: my ears. Choose how I listen, so you can talk instead of type. Live voice, a hands-free conversation, works with any provider here that has an API key; the browser's own voice works for dictation and read-aloud only.
say.listenTeam: Last one: my ears. Choose how I listen, so you can talk instead of type. Live voice works with any provider here that has an API key, not the browser's own voice. Voice is shared by everyone on your team.
say.listenConnect: Paste your {provider} API key so I can turn your speech into text.

SetupChat.configFile: Every choice here can also live in ~/.amiro/amiro.toml (every option: amiro.example.toml next to the app).
SetupChat.runAgain: Run this setup again any time from Admin → General.

greet.title: Let's bring your agent to life
greet.body: A few small choices, one at a time, and this agent becomes yours: how it looks, how it thinks, what it can see and what it can do.

look.title: Give your agent a face you'll love
look.body: This little character lives in your sidebar and wears headphones when you talk to it. Pick the colour and shape that feel like yours.
look.p1: The colour tints the whole app
look.p2: Four shapes, each with its own charm
look.p3: Restyle it any time on the Agent page

prompt.title: Every agent starts with a few words
prompt.body: Before every conversation your agent reads two short files. They are who it is and how it works. Nothing hidden: this is the whole of it.
prompt.p2: SOUL.md: its habits, grown as it learns you
prompt.p3: Plain text you can read any time

personality.title: How should it talk to you?
personality.body: Warm companion or sharp operator? Playful or serious? Tune the dials until it sounds like someone you want to work with.

provider.title: Choose a brain for your agent to think with
provider.body: Your agent thinks with an AI model from a provider you choose. Bring an API key, sign in with an account you already have, or run a model on your own machine.
provider.p2: Keys stay encrypted on this machine

search.title: Let your agent see the live web
search.body: With web search your agent can look things up as they happen today: news, docs, prices, answers it doesn't already know.
search.p1: Free engines need no key at all
search.p2: Sources it can cite back to you

connectors.title: Give your agent the superpowers it needs
connectors.body: Connect the apps you live in so your agent can act there too: read the inbox, file the ticket, update the doc, post the message.
connectors.p2: Any MCP server, local or remote
connectors.p3: It asks before anything leaves the machine

voice.title: Let your agent speak
voice.body: Give your agent a voice to read its answers aloud while you cook, drive or just look away from the screen.
voice.p1: Read answers aloud, one tap away
voice.p2: Pick the voice you like best
voice.p3: The browser's own voice needs no key

done.title: Your agent is ready to work
done.body: That's everything. Say hi, hand it a task, and see what it can do. Anything you skipped is waiting in the setup checklist.
done.p2: Tune it further on its pages
done.p3: Run setup again from Admin → General

listen.title: Let your agent listen
listen.body: Talk instead of typing: dictate a message, or hold a live, hands-free conversation where it answers out loud.
listen.p2: Live voice with any keyed provider

SetupChat.liveVoiceReady: Live voice is ready: a hands-free conversation that listens with {stt} and speaks with {tts}.
SetupChat.liveVoiceNeeds: Live voice, a hands-free conversation, works with any speaking and listening provider that has an API key: OpenAI, Deepgram, Groq, ElevenLabs and more. The browser's built-in voice works for read-aloud and dictation, not live voice.
SetupChat.alsoListen: Use {provider} to listen too (speech to text)

Channels.title: Outside Amiro
Channels.description: Important notifications can also reach you on Telegram, Slack or Discord. Amiro sends them with the bot you connected in Channels, to your own account on your contact card in Contacts, once you verify it with a code.

step.owner_only: Only the owner's notifications go outside Amiro

Channels.whatGoes: Routine updates stay in Amiro. Urgent things that need you, and test notifications, go to every ready channel. Chat replies always stay in Amiro.

Connection.title: This app is connected to

PhoneAccess.title: Phone access
PhoneAccess.description: Let paired phones reach this computer over your Wi-Fi network. Only devices you approve can use it.

PhoneAccess.warning: Traffic on your network is not encrypted. Use this on a network you trust, or reach this computer through a private network such as Tailscale.

Pair.title: Connect to Amiro
Pair.description: Enter the address of the Amiro you want to use. You only do this once on this device.
Pair.waitingDescription: Approve this device on your Amiro to finish connecting.
Pair.serverHint: For example https://amiro.example.com, or the Wi-Fi address shown in Settings → Devices.
Pair.approveAt: Or go to {address} in any browser, sign in, and enter this code.
Pair.approveOnComputer: On the computer running Amiro, you can also approve it in Settings → Devices.
Pair.waiting: Waiting for approval · code expires in {time}
Pair.denied: This device was denied. Ask again if that was a mistake.
Pair.expired: The code expired before it was approved. Get a new one.
Pair.badAddress: Enter an address like https://amiro.example.com or http://192.168.1.5:8790
Pair.httpsNeeded: Use an https:// address. Plain http:// only works on your own network (Wi-Fi, Tailscale).
Pair.unreachable: Could not reach that address. Check it, and that Amiro is running there (on Wi-Fi: that phone access is on).

Approve.title: Connect a device
Approve.description: Enter the code shown on the device that wants to use your Amiro.
